notes.title: Devlog #3: 2024 Update and the Future of Reborn a Zombie
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44801201/99086fff497ad6f4e56e5adf2af6e00d6cb47dcc.png[/img]

A lot has changed in my life in 2024, but I’m happy to say things have been improving. Now, let’s dive into the news:

[h1]Reborn a Zombie: Major Update[/h1]
[b]When?[/b]
First half of 2025

[b]What’s new?[/b]
[list]
[*] The game will be playable in French.
[*] Added game controller support.
[*] A post-credits teaser that will tie into Reborn a Zombie 2.
[/list]
I personally handled the translation, and while it was a lot of work, it was also a lot of fun. I hope this will allow more people to enjoy the story.

[b]Reborn a Zombie 2 is also expected to receive a French translation.[/b]

[h1]Reborn a Zombie 2: Entwined Hearts is Progressing, but There’s Still Much to Do[/h1]
[b]When?[/b]
Tentatively 2026

[b]Why the delay?[/b]
Depression.
I have a full-time job that demands a lot from me, and this passion project demands even more.

That said, I’m considering running a playtest to gather feedback on the first half of Reborn a Zombie 2. If you’re interested, join our Discord!

[h1]The Future of Reborn a Zombie and Asminae Games: Magii Archives[/h1]
Initially, I planned to announce future games following Reborn a Zombie 2. However, the time required to create each game has made me cautious. What’s the point of announcing games if they might not be delivered?

That said, here’s what I can share:

[b]Reborn a Zombie is part of Magii Archives[/b], a shared universe encompassing all my future games. Think of it as a mix between the Marvel Cinematic Universe and Terry Pratchett’s Discworld in terms of continuity and shared universe.

[b]Each new entry will stand alone[/b] but contribute to expanding this universe. Some will progress an overarching narrative, while others will explore fascinating aspects of this world.

[b]Reborn a Zombie is the first series in this universe.[/b]

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[b]Can I play games in any order I want?[/b]
Unless a game is a direct sequel, [b]each story is designed to be enjoyable as a standalone[/b]. However, playing other games in the Magii Archives will add depth to the experience, as the lore and major events will have repercussion across multiple entries.

[b]Are all Magii Archives games going to be kinetic, slice-of-life visual novels?[/b]
Not always. While the focus is on storytelling, I’m open to experimenting with gameplay styles.

[b]Are all Magii Archives games going to be trans-themed?[/b]
Reborn a Zombie was born out of my desire to share my experience as a trans person through storytelling. But writing is my passion, and I’m excited to explore a wide range of ideas and experiences in this universe.

[h1]What’s Next?[/h1]
I won’t announce a game until its script is 100% complete. This ensures I can deliver high-quality stories and avoid making false promises.

One such project was Lamia Panic. Although the script was completed in March 2023, its flaws outweighed its strengths. I decided it was best used for worldbuilding instead of a standalone release.

That said, Reborn a Zombie 3 is very likely to happen. No promises yet, but it’s high on my list.

[h1]I Want More![/h1]
Thank you for your support! The best way to stay updated is through my Discord server. There, you’ll find news on current projects and the Magii Archives universe.

I’m so excited to share these stories with you. I’ve worked in the game industry for five years. Yet, Reborn a Zombie 2 is my most ambitious project, and I’m incredibly proud of it. I hope you’ll enjoy the story as much as I’ve enjoyed creating it.

– Asminae and the Asminae Games Team

notes.title: Announcing Reborn a Zombie 2: Entwined Hearts
notes.content:
I am excited to announce that [b]Reborn a Zombie 2: Entwined Hearts is now officially in development![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43903920/42bb3ad683616f9864ec3000570073ede609d3ff.jpg[/img]
[i]Gorgeous artwork made by Betto, you can find their [url=https://twitter.com/BetrunkenH/status/1730548976649228559]twitter here[/url][/i]

Reborn a Zombie 2 is a direct sequel, set a couple of months after Dawn's transformation, and will heavily emphasize Lucia's family.

[b]You can [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2641800/Reborn_a_Zombie_2_Entwined_Hearts/]wishlist the game and get notified when it releases![/url][/b]

[b]Major feature includes:[/b]
[list]
[*]-About 40k words (3-4 hours of playtime)
[*]A story that explores Vulcan's past and expands on the world of Reborn a Zombie.
[*] A lot of demons, dragons, zombies, and also vampires?!
[/list]
[b]FAQ[/b]
[i]Do I need to play the first game?[/i]
[b]Yes.[/b] The good news is, [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2283350/Reborn_A_Zombie/]Reborn a Zombie is free![/url][/b]

[i]The CG above looks different. Will there be a shift in the game's art style?[/i]
If you're wondering why Dawn looks so different in the CG, you'll have to play the game!

[i]When will the game be released?[/i]
We hope to deliver the game in early 2025.

We will make more announcements down the road!
Thank you all for making this journey possible.

notes.title: Devlog #2 The writing of Reborn a Zombie!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43903920/07e86bb23391f211dd01418d94ebc19d10bb987e.png[/img]
[h1]The writing of Reborn a Zombie![/h1]
[i]This is the second Devlog following the launch of my debut game: Reborn a Zombie![/i]

[i]Reborn a Zombie was released on August 7th. It’s a fantasy, slice-of-life visual in a world where Vampires, succubuses, and all sorts of magic creatures now coexist with humans.
The development of Reborn a Zombie took 20 months and was a story of its own, one that I want to share with you now. Join me in this journey of making Reborn a Zombie! [/i]

[h2]Unfulfilled creativity[/h2]
After the release of Raz, I couldn’t stop talking about it. I was so proud! There was some great reaction, and one of them struck me in particular: [b]“It’s incredible that you managed to get your project done. To write what you wanted to write”[/b]

The thing is, while it’s easy to see what has been done, It’s as easy to forget how long this project wasn’t anything.
I’d like to share my first attempt at making a game, doing “my own thing” and such. And it starts with…

[h3]A whole lot of nothing but fear[/h3]
When I was younger, I’d spent days after days dreaming of this unique (was it?) world and amazing (it wasn’t!) stories that’d unfold. And they’d play in my head and they were perfect.

I grew up and the desire to create never left me. I figured what I wanted to do: To create a story and present it as a visual novel! 

The thing is, I knew nothing about the craft. I was afraid to put myself out there. At this point, I had several scripts started, and none were finished. I was afraid of those stories. “What if they turned out bad?”. The insecurity was paralyzing.

The turning point happened when I played [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1502520/The_Mermaid_of_Zennor/]The Mermaid of Zennor[/url] by Ebi-Hime. I was struck by the simplicity of the game in a structural sense, yet how powerful the story was. It got me quickly invested in searching for more of their work, and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/developer/ebi-hime]there was a lot to enjoy.[/url] (You should check it out too!)

[h3]Create something that matters[/h3]
The mermaid of Zennor deeply resonated with me. I realized that for me to make one story. Just one. [b]It had to be something that mattered to me beyond anything else.[/b] Let’s forget about marketing considerations, cost, time, and energy.  [b]Just for one moment in your life: Be a writer.[/b]

It took 6 months to get a script version I’d consider finished. The experience was exhausting, and filled with joy and tears. I understood that writing was deeply important to me. The process, the journey itself was too much fun, I couldn’t stop writing, and never will.
If you’re an aspiring writer or artist: I want you to find your voice. To find your joy in your self-expression.

[h2]Learning the craft[/h2]
There are so many possibilities when it comes to writing a story. So many narrative structures (expanded even further with a medium such as video games!) and words, concepts, worldbuilding, and philosophical ideas!

I am by no means a seasoned, experienced writer, but everyone learns to figure out what works for them and what doesn’t. I want to offer some of the hindsight I learned while writing.

[h3]Worldbuilding - No plan was the best plan[/h3]
Something that stopped me for too long was worldbuilding. I knew I was writing a fantasy story, but I was stuck with the idea that I couldn’t start writing a single word if this world wasn’t fully defined first. I managed to write much, much more when I decided to throw all my anxiety away and just start writing. 

I had two core ideas established so far: Magiis came from another world and Providence was the bridge between our world and theirs, and [b]it was all that was needed! [/b]Everything else was intuitively crafted to fit the story that was developing at the time.

There are people out there who love worldbuilding: Good for them! However, I’ve seen as many pantsers and plotters just never making progress because they’d get stuck in the nitty-gritty details. 

Here are the problems I faced:

[list]
[*] It was overwhelming. There’s virtually no limit on how deeper we can go in establishing this world,
[*] A lot of this wasn’t useful. Why talk about the Old World’s economy when it bears little weight in the story and I honestly don’t know much about world economics in the first place?
[*] I feared that I’d get stuck. Establishing a magic system without knowing what sorts of stories it can support, for instance, was scary. I didn’t know what I was going to write about!
[*] Worldbuilding is essential. Harry Potter wouldn’t be Harry Potter without its world-building and fantastic visual direction. It carries so much power, charm, and intrigue to this world. But it has to serve the story. Not the other way around!
[/list]

[h3]Explore the limits[/h3]
Another problem was this question of “Writing myself into a corner.” as in [b]“What if I establish rules or concepts that get in the way in the future”?[/b]  After all, if characters can use magic to -say- teleport, there’s no dangerous situation they can be put in: They could just teleport away!

To prepare for this, I decided to establish strong limits for each element I’d bring to the table. Let’s explore the idea of Alchemy.

[i]Spoiler alert from here![/i]

Alchemy is the main magic system present in Reborn a Zombie, but it has several issues that need to be addressed. [b]Alchemy is very powerful.[/b] Which itself isn’t a problem! [b]The real issue was:[/b] Its underlying concept -Any ingredient is used for its meaning- is not difficult to understand, Vulcan was even able to make those potions. [b]Anyone can make any potion they want if there’s no limit to this concept.[/b]

[b]Here’s my solution: Establish “ingredient scarcity”.[/b] To create the ultimate transforming potion, it’d need an ultimate-level of ingredient. [b]This is why The Alchemist became an ingredient and had to die[/b]. It even brought Archi to a whole new level of evil that was delightful to write (Kehkehkeh!).

Because RaZ was very short, I barely scratched the surface of a concept like this. Alchemy has a lot of great potential, and I know I will use it further!

[h3]Write a lot, and start as many projects as you need![/h3]
[i]Shouldn’t it be “finish a project first before starting a new one?”[/i]

After finishing Reborn’s editing, I was proud of the story as a whole, but a lot of scenes felt shallow. Unable to find a solution, I went on to write more story ideas I had.

Bittersweet bite was a vampire lesbian story, that’d follow the story of the protagonist who bites and transforms the love interest into a vampii, and explores Vampii’s life and culture.

 Lamia Panic was a mystery rom-com exploring the history and bloodline of Lamias. Both were exciting and promising stories. I even commissioned logos!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43903920/d31673d409fb7523dbc6c8b17a894ec251b9dabf.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43903920/febd2eb0379fb3711dfc15cccbaa44de5f185c85.png[/img]
BB was never finished. Lamia Panic’s story was mediocre. None will become full-fledged visual novels, but both were fantastic learning experiences and great world-building material! 

This significantly improved some of the scenes as the characters can now mention things far more specific to this world! While worldbuilding only what is needed for a single script is a good way to get things started, “useless worldbuilding” is also very useful to make the world feel alive!
For instance, Bixbite the vampii didn’t exist in the original RaZ script. But it is now a well-established character, and now vampiis exist in RaZ!

What’s that? Someone in the crowd as a question!
[i]You say the vampiis exist in Dawn’s story. But we only barely hear about them in-game![/i]
That, my friend, is about to change. [b]But I can’t talk about it just yet![/b]

The next devlog will develop a wide variety of topics I haven’t covered so far. It will also be the opportunity to answer questions you may have about the project. Put those questions down and I’ll take the time to answer them in devlog#3!

notes.title: Reborn a zombie - Progress update #2
notes.content:
Hi there! It's been a while, but I come with good news!
The game's development has been progressing well, and we have an almost-set-in-stone release date.

The game was originally planned to release during pride month, but there's no bad time to be proud! I'm happy to announce that [b]Reborn a zombie will be available starting August 7th for free![/b]

This mean the game is almost ready for everyone to play.
Let's look at what's left to do:
- 1 CG
- All music will be implemented in the following weeks, and I commissioned a sound designer to help out with the sound effects. It's the first time I get to work on SFX so it's an exciting moment!
-  Some polish on the visuals, text and acting.

I plan to add achievements and some level of compatibility with the Steam Deck further down the line. In the demo, the game interface is kinda broken. I can't promise to make the game fully compatible (as I'm still very much a novice when it comes to technical features like this) but I can say for certain: The game will be playable!

That's all for now. I am waiting for you on August, 7th!

Asminae

notes.title: Reborn a zombie - Progress update
notes.content:
Greetings! Here's an update over the progress made since the release of the demo of Reobnr a zombie!

-Writing: 100%
-Character Art: 100%
-BG Art: 85%
-Programming: 80%
-CG Art: 70%

[b]The game is playable from start to finish.[/b] Implementation is going to be the last major step before release. No room for improvisation here, Reborn a Zombie will release!

[b]All the background art is done![/b] The only thing left is to add visual effects!

[b]The character design for all characters is also done[/b], which is the opportunity to give you a quick preview of another character!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43903920/c2579834f70821be68159435e59989bf28c67cdd.png[/img]

Who is this mysterious Ronin? Why does she seem to resent Vulcan? Play the game to find out!

Reborn's demo took 8 months to release. However it also taught me many things, including how to manage a healthy workflow for future releases. In comparison to the demo, the full release is going far more smoothly! This is something I'd like to share more insight at a later time, probably in the form of Devlogs.
Thank you for reading, I'll be back soon with more to share!

-Asminae
